Do not use `in args` membership-only assertions in the new test; use exact equality including the empty-flags baseline.
procedure: Locate debug_flag_error() in qutebrowser/qutebrowser.py. Append the new flag name to the valid_flags list; otherwise argparse rejects it.
In the same function, add a 'name: description' line to the docstring flag list, matching the style of existing entries such as 'stack: Enable Chromium stack logging.'.
Locate the _qtwebengine_args(namespace) generator in qutebrowser/config/configinit.py.
Add a branch shaped like `if '<flag>' in namespace.debug_flags:` that yields each Chromium switch with a separate `yield`, e.g. '--enable-logging' and '--v=1'.
Put the branch next to the existing debug_flags handling (after the 'stack' block) and before the settings-dict processing, so argument order stays predictable.
In TestQtArgs in tests/unit/config/test_configinit.py, add a test parametrized over ([], []) and (['--debug-flag', '<flag>'], [expected switches]).
In that test, monkeypatch configinit.objects.backend to usertypes.Backend.QtWebEngine.
In that test, assert `configinit.qt_args(parsed) == [sys.argv[0]] + expected`, an exact list comparison that also checks for no stray args.

trigger.task_type: Add --debug-flag <name> that toggles Chromium/QtWebEngine command-line switches

validation: Run `pytest tests/unit/config/test_configinit.py -k TestQtArgs`.
Run `pytest tests/unit/test_qutebrowser.py` if it exists, plus any argparse tests.
Manually run `python -m qutebrowser --debug-flag <flag> --debug` and confirm the switches appear in the logged Qt args.
Confirm an invalid flag name still raises an argparse error.

name: qutebrowser-add-qwebsettings-boolean-option
negative_constraints: 不要只改 configdata 而漏掉 websettings 映射，否则选项存在但不生效。
不要只加映射而不在 configdata 中声明，否则会出现配置校验或查找错误。
不要为布尔 WebAttribute 新写 setter 类或直接调用 QWebSettings.globalSettings()，应复用 Attribute。
不要把默认值设为 'true'，否则会改变用户的现有行为，除非任务明确要求。
不要使用 snake_case 或驼峰命名选项，仓库约定为 kebab-case。
不要启用注释中的其他实验性 attribute（如 accelerated-compositing），除非任务明确要求。
procedure: 先确认该功能在 QtWebKit 中有对应的 QWebSettings.WebAttribute 枚举。smooth scrolling 对应 QWebSettings.ScrollAnimatorEnabled。可在 websettings.py 中被注释掉的条目里查找候选项。
在 configdata.py 的 data() 中找到语义相关的 section。网页渲染/行为类选项放在 'general' 等 css-media-type 所在的 section。
在该 section 中新增一个 kebab-case 的 ('<name>', SettingValue(typ.Bool(), 'false'), '<一句话 docstring>') 条目。默认值写成字符串 'false'，以保持现有行为不变。
在 websettings.py 的 MAPPINGS 中，找到与 configdata section 同名的 key，在其下添加同名映射 '<name>': Attribute(QWebSettings.<EnumName>)。
布尔型 attribute 直接复用现有的 Attribute 包装类。只有非布尔的 getter/setter 才使用 Setter 或 NullStringSetter。
保持两个文件中的选项名与 section 完全一致。websettings 会按 section/option 双键查找映射。
validation: 运行现有测试（如 tox / pytest 的 config 相关测试），确认 configdata 能正常加载且没有重复键。
检查 MAPPINGS 中新 key 所在的 section 名与 configdata 中的 section 一致。
如仓库有从 configdata 自动生成的文档（settings.asciidoc / 文档生成脚本），重新生成或确认 CI 文档检查通过。
手动测试：执行 :set <section> <name> true，确认 QWebSettings.globalSettings().testAttribute(...) 的值随之变化。

name: qutebrowser-add-short-cli-option-alias
negative_constraints: Do not change dest names. The derived attribute names (args.debug, args.debug_flags) are used across the codebase.
Do not reuse a short letter that is already taken, and do not pick one that could clash with Qt arguments passed through.
Do not move the option to a different argument group, and do not change the order of the group's options in help output.
Do not change action='append' semantics. Repeating -D must still accumulate flags.
procedure: Find the existing long option in get_argparser() in qutebrowser/qutebrowser.py. Note which argument group it belongs to, e.g. the 'debug' group.
Before choosing a short flag, list every add_argument call on the parser and on all of its groups. Make sure the short letter is unused. Case matters: -d and -D are different flags.
Add the short flag as the first positional string in the same add_argument call, e.g. debug.add_argument('-d', '--debug', ...). Do not create a second add_argument call.

Leave dest, action, type, default and help unchanged. For example, --debug-flag must keep dest='debug_flags', action='append', default=[] and type=debug_flag_error, so code that reads args.debug and args.debug_flags keeps working.

Keep lines under the repo's line-length limit (79 chars). When the call grows, rewrap the keyword arguments and split the help string with implicit string concatenation, following the existing style in the file.

trigger.task_type: Add short option alias for existing qutebrowser CLI argument

validation: Run python -m qutebrowser --help and confirm '-d, --debug' and '-D DEBUG_FLAGS, --debug-flag DEBUG_FLAGS' are listed.
Parse ['-d', '-D', 'x', '-D', 'y'] with get_argparser() and assert debug is True and debug_flags is ['x', 'y'] (with valid flag names).
Confirm that an invalid -D value still raises an error via debug_flag_error.
Run the existing unit tests and flake8/pylint on qutebrowser/qutebrowser.py.

name: qutebrowser-avoid-except-shadowing-param
negative_constraints: 不要重命名函数参数 `e`。它是 Qt 事件处理方法签名的一部分，子类和调用方可能依赖它。
不要用 `# pylint: disable` 压制该警告，重命名才是正确修复。
不要改动异常处理逻辑、日志文本或返回值，例如 QKeySequence.NoMatch。
不要顺带重构无关代码。
procedure: 定位 pylint 报告的 except 子句，确认 `except X as <name>` 中的 <name> 与函数参数或外层局部变量重名。在 keyinput 代码里，Qt 事件参数常用 `e` 命名，例如 handle(self, e)。
把异常变量改成不冲突的名字。本仓库的惯例是 `ex`，也可以用 `err` 或 `exc`。
同步更新 except 块内对该异常变量的所有引用，例如 format(ex)。
检查同一函数中 except 块之后是否还用到原参数，例如 `e`。Python 3 会在 except 结束时 del 掉异常变量，重名会让原参数被删除，这是潜在的运行时 bug，不只是风格问题。
在同一文件和同一模块的其他 handler 中搜索 `except .* as e:` 加 `(self, e)` 的组合，确认是否有同类问题，并一并修复。
validation: 对修改的文件运行 pylint（例如 `tox -e pylint` 或 `pylint qutebrowser/keyinput/basekeyparser.py`），确认告警消失。
运行 flake8 / tox -e flake8，确认没有新的告警。
运行现有单元测试：pytest tests/unit/keyinput。
人工确认 except 块内部已不再引用旧名称。

name: qutebrowser-backend-search-dedup-parity
negative_constraints: Do not set self.search_displayed or self.text before the duplicate check; the early return depends on the previous state.
Do not change the dedup condition. It is text equality plus search_displayed. Do not add ignore_case or reverse to it unless the reference backend does the same.
Do not hoist the guard into AbstractSearch while doing this task. The accepted change keeps per-backend parity with minimal diff.
Do not invoke result_cb or start a find when the search is ignored. The reference returns silently with only a debug log.
Do not leave any reference to the removed constant (for example `_NO_FLAGS`) in either backend.
Do not move backend-specific Qt classes such as QWebPage or QWebEnginePage into browsertab.py.
procedure: Open both backends' Search classes: WebEngineSearch.search in webenginetab.py and WebKitSearch.search in webkittab.py. Treat the backend that already has the behavior as the reference implementation.

Copy the reference guard verbatim to the top of WebKitSearch.search. Put it before any state is mutated: `if self.text == text and self.search_displayed: log.webview.debug("Ignoring duplicate search request for {}".format(text)); return`.

Move `self.search_displayed = True` so it runs after the guard and after `self.text = text`. If the flag is set first, the guard compares against an already-overwritten state and suppresses even the first search.
Leave flag computation (QWebPage.FindWrapsAroundDocument / FindCaseSensitively / FindBackward) and the find call after the guard, unchanged.

Make the explanatory comment identical in both backends and backend-neutral: '# Don't go to next entry on duplicate search'. Remove any comment that names the other backend as the source, such as '(webkit behavior)', because that becomes stale once the behavior is shared.
When fixing per-search state such as `_flags`, `text` or wrap/match data in one backend's Search class, open the matching class in the other backend.
List every place that initializes or resets the state: `__init__`, and the start of `search()` before new flags are built up.
Route all initializations and resets through one helper per class, such as `_empty_flags()`, so no stale reference or alternate path remains.
Keep WebEngine-specific extras unchanged, for example `_wrap_handler.reset_match_data()` and `flag_wrap`. Change only the shared concern.

trigger.task_type: Implement deduplication of searches on webkit

validation: Run the existing search tests, for example `pytest tests/end2end/features/search.feature` for both backends (--qute-bdd-webengine and the default webkit).
Manual check: run :search foo and then :search foo again. The current match should not advance. The debug log should show 'Ignoring duplicate search request for foo'.
Run :search foo, then :search bar, then :search foo. Each change of text must trigger a new search.
After clear_search sets search_displayed to False, :search foo must search again.
Run flake8/pylint on the touched files. Keep line wrapping consistent with the reference.

name: qutebrowser-binding-precedence-over-count-digits
negative_constraints: 不要在配置校验层继续拒绝纯数字或含数字的按键序列，否则用户无法绑定数字。
不要把 count 检测放在 _match_key 和 key_mappings 匹配之前，否则数字绑定永远不会触发。
不要去掉 '空 count 时 0 不作为 count' 的守卫，也不要去掉 _supports_count 检查。
dry_run 模式下不要修改 self._count 或其他解析器状态。
不要绕过 key_mappings。映射后的序列必须先于 count 回退参与匹配。
procedure: 在 qutebrowser/keyinput/basekeyparser.py 的 BaseKeyParser 按键处理方法里找到 count 分支。这个分支的条件是 txt.isdigit() and self._supports_count，命中后把数字累加到 self._count 并返回 ExactMatch。
把这个 count 分支整体移到匹配流程之后。顺序改为：先调用 self._sequence.append_event(e) 并用 _match_key(sequence) 直接匹配；未命中时用 config.val.bindings.key_mappings 映射后再匹配；两者都返回 QKeySequence.NoMatch 时才把数字当作 count。
count 分支保留原有守卫：txt 必须是单个数字，必须 _supports_count，且当前 count 为空时 '0' 不能开始一个 count。只有非 dry_run 时才修改 self._count，dry_run 时直接返回 ExactMatch。
在 qutebrowser/config/configtypes.py 的 Key.to_py 中删除拒绝无修饰键 Qt.Key_1..Key_9 的校验（报错信息为 'Numbers are reserved for counts!'）。只保留 KeySequence.parse，并继续把 KeyParseError 转换为 configexc.ValidationError。
如有需要，删除 configtypes.py 中因此不再使用的 Qt 导入。
更新测试：在 tests/unit/keyinput/conftest.py 的 BINDINGS['normal'] 中加入 '1' 之类的数字绑定；在 test_configtypes.py 中把 '1' 和 'a1' 从 test_to_py_invalid 移到 test_to_py_valid。
增加 keyparser 测试，覆盖三种情况：已绑定的数字直接执行命令；未绑定的数字仍作为 count 前缀；绑定了 '0' 时，count 为空的 '0' 执行绑定，已有 count 时的 '0' 追加到 count。

trigger.task_type: Allow to bind numbers in keybindings

validation: pytest tests/unit/config/test_configtypes.py -k TestKey
pytest tests/unit/keyinput/
确认 count 行为未退化：未绑定数字后接命令（如 '5j'）仍以 count=5 执行。
确认已绑定的数字和 key_mappings 映射得到的序列优先于 count 生效。

name: qutebrowser-boolean-option-css-injection-polarity
negative_constraints: Do not change the injected scrollbar CSS selector or its values while fixing the polarity.
Do not rename the option or change its default to hide the logic bug.
Do not use truthiness on an option whose type might be a non-boolean string.
Do not change the order in which the user stylesheet file is read and the extra CSS is appended.
procedure: Open qutebrowser/browser/shared.py and find get_user_stylesheet(). It reads the CSS file set by content.user_stylesheet, then appends extra CSS based on config options.

Check that each condition matches what the option means. scrolling.bar=True means 'show the scrollbar'. The CSS that hides the scrollbar (html > ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 0px; height: 0px; }) must only be appended when the option is False, i.e. under `if not config.val.scrolling.bar:`.
Fix only the boolean check (add or remove `not`). Leave the CSS string and how it is concatenated unchanged.
Check the option's description in qutebrowser/config/configdata.yml to confirm what True and False mean. Do not guess the polarity from the option's name.
If option values can now be tri-state or strings (for example 'always'/'never'/'when-searching'), use explicit comparisons such as `== 'never'` instead of truthiness checks.
Check that whatever re-applies the stylesheet when scrolling.bar changes still fires, so the fix takes effect immediately.
Add or adjust a unit test that monkeypatches config_stub.val.scrolling.bar to True and to False. Assert that '::-webkit-scrollbar' is absent when True and present when False.
validation: Run the existing tests: pytest tests/unit/browser -k stylesheet.
Unit-test get_user_stylesheet with scrolling.bar=True and with False, and assert the hide-scrollbar CSS appears only when False.
Manual check: run `:set scrolling.bar false` and confirm the scrollbar disappears; run `:set scrolling.bar true` and confirm it comes back.

name: qutebrowser-bump-copyright-year-pair
negative_constraints: 不要改动 vim modeline、GPL 正文或任何代码逻辑。
不要修改起始年份,也不要把范围改成单个年份。
不要只改源码文件而遗漏对应的测试文件。新文件(如 keyutils 及其测试)通常是成对复制旧模板产生的,因此会成对过期。
不要为纯版权年份调整添加 changelog 条目。
procedure: 定位目标模块头部第3行的 '# Copyright <start>-<end> Florian Bruhin (The Compiler) <[REDACTED_EMAIL]>'。header 结构为: vim modeline、空行、Copyright 行、'#'、'# This file is part of qutebrowser.'。
只修改结束年份。例如 2014-2017 改为 2014-2018。起始年份、作者名和邮箱保持原样。
定位源码模块对应的单元测试文件。路径映射规则为 qutebrowser/<pkg>/<mod>.py -> tests/unit/<pkg>/test_<mod>.py,例如 keyinput/keyutils.py -> tests/unit/keyinput/test_keyutils.py。对测试文件的 header 做同样的年份修改。
用 grep 检查同目录下其他文件,例如 git grep -n 'Copyright 2014-2017' qutebrowser/keyinput tests/unit/keyinput,确认是否还有新增或被遗漏的旧年份文件。是否一并修改由任务范围决定。
validation: git diff 中每个文件只有 Copyright 那一行发生变化。
git grep -n 'Copyright 2014-2017' 在目标源码和测试文件中无结果。
运行 scripts/dev/check_coverage 或 pylint 的 copyright 相关检查(若存在),或运行 pytest tests/unit/keyinput,确认没有语法破坏。

name: qutebrowser-chromium-version-docstring-patch-update
negative_constraints: 不要修改 _chromium_version() 的函数逻辑、user-agent 解析或任何非 docstring 的代码。
不要保留已被取代的中间 patch 行。约定是每个分支只保留一条最新的 'Security fixes up to' 行。
不要猜测 Chromium 版本号或日期。应来自 Qt 官方发布说明或 QtWebEngine 的 chromium 子模块信息。
不要更改基础 Chromium 版本行(即 'X.0.Y.Z (date)' 这一行),除非确认它本身有误。
这类纯 docstring 改动不需要新增测试或 changelog 条目。
procedure: 定位 qutebrowser/utils/version.py 中 _chromium_version() 的 docstring。它是一张 Qt minor 版本到 Chromium 版本的对照表,只是文档,不影响代码逻辑。
对每个发布了新 patch 的 Qt 分支,找到它的行 'X.Y.Z: Security fixes up to <chromium version> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)'。LTS 分支(如 5.9、5.12)下面带有 patch 行。
用最新的 patch 行替换旧行:写入新的 patch 版本号(如 5.12.3)、它所包含的 Chromium 安全修复版本(如 73.0.3683.75)和对应的 Chromium 发布日期。
如果同一 Qt 分支下列了多条中间 patch 行(如 5.12.1、5.12.2),把它们合并成一条最新的行,只保留最新 patch 的信息。
保持对齐格式不变:13 个空格缩进,'(LTS)' 标记放在基础版本行前面,并保留 '(in development)' 等注释。
如果开发中分支(如 Qt 5.13)有确认的 Chromium 版本或日期,一并核对更新。
validation: 运行 flake8 或 pylint 检查 qutebrowser/utils/version.py,确认 docstring 改动没有破坏缩进或行长限制。
运行现有测试 pytest tests/unit/utils/test_version.py,确认没有回归。
人工核对:每个 LTS 分支只有一行 'Security fixes up to',且版本号与日期与 Qt 发布说明一致。

name: qutebrowser-chromium-version-docstring-update
negative_constraints: Do not change the function's logic, its regex, or its return behavior. This is a comment-only change.
Do not reformat, reorder, or re-indent other entries in the table.
Do not add a changelog entry or tests for a docstring-only data update.
Do not drop the (LTS) marker or other annotations on existing entries.
Do not use a shortened Chromium version such as '72'. Patch lines need the full four-part version.
procedure: Locate the docstring of _chromium_version() in qutebrowser/utils/version.py. It holds a Qt-to-Chromium mapping table.
Find the block for the Qt minor series that got the new patch release, for example 'Qt 5.12: Chromium 69'.
Add one new line right after the last existing patch line of that series. Use the format '<qt.patch>: Security fixes up to <full chromium version> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)'.
Copy the column alignment of the neighboring lines exactly. Patch lines are indented to line up under the base Chromium version.
Keep lines in ascending patch order, so 5.12.1 comes before 5.12.2.
Take the Chromium version and date from the official QtWebEngine release notes or Chromium release data. Use the date of the Chromium security release, not the Qt release date.
If the change is about a Qt version still in development, update only its '(in development)' line. Do not invent patch lines for it.
validation: Check that the diff touches only docstring lines inside _chromium_version().
Run flake8/pylint on qutebrowser/utils/version.py to confirm there are no line-length or whitespace problems.
Run pytest tests/unit/utils/test_version.py to confirm nothing is broken.
Visually confirm the new line's column alignment matches the line above it.

name: qutebrowser-classify-sqlite-error-as-environmental
negative_constraints: Do not add the code as an int. Compare as a string, because nativeErrorCode() returns a string.
Do not add codes that point to programming errors, such as SQLITE_ERROR (1), SQLITE_MISUSE (21) or SQLITE_RANGE. Those must still raise SqlBugError so they show up in crash reports.
Do not change the list order or delete existing entries (5, 8, 13).
Do not try to repair or recover the database as part of this change. The scope is error classification only.
procedure: Open qutebrowser/misc/sql.py and find the class SqliteError(SqlError). In its error-classification logic, locate the environmental_errors list.
That list holds native SQLite result codes as strings, compared against QSqlError.nativeErrorCode(). Find the numeric code for the new error. SQLITE_CORRUPT is '11'.
Add the code as a string literal, e.g. '11'. Insert it so the list stays in numeric order (between '8' and '13').
Copy the existing comment style on the new line: `'11',  # SQLITE_CORRUPT`.
Change only the classification list. Do not touch the existing driver-message fallback (the init()-time error checks after the list) or the code that raises SqlEnvironmentError vs SqlBugError.

If tests/unit/misc/test_sql.py has a parametrized test over environmental and bug error codes, add the new code to the environmental cases. If the project keeps a changelog (doc/changelog.asciidoc), consider adding a short entry saying corrupt databases now produce a user-facing error instead of a crash report.

trigger.task_type: Add SQLITE_CORRUPT to environmental SQL errors

validation: Run the existing tests: pytest tests/unit/misc/test_sql.py.
Write a test that mocks QSqlError with nativeErrorCode '11', or add a parametrized case for it. Assert that raise_sqlite_error / SqliteError.from_query produces SqlEnvironmentError, not SqlBugError.
Run flake8/pylint on qutebrowser/misc/sql.py to check comment alignment and style.

name: qutebrowser-command-argv-list-signature
negative_constraints: Do not mix the *args convention with a list-passing convention between parse and the Command methods.
Do not blindly emit self.signal.emit(*argv) in the base class. pyqtSignal arity and types are fixed per subclass, so the mapping must be explicit in each subclass.
Do not change TypeError to another exception type without also updating the except clause in CommandParser.parse.
Do not remove the NotImplementedError guard for commands without a signal.
Do not declare a parameterized pyqtSignal while relying on the base run. It emits with no arguments and fails at runtime.
Do not index argv beyond what nargs guarantees.
不要让 KeyError 继续往外抛, 也不要在 emit 之后接着往下执行 parse。
不要在 CommandParser 里直接导入或调用 statusbar 控件, 必须通过 Qt 信号解耦, 并在 app.py 中完成连接。
不要用 print 或 logging 来代替面向用户的状态栏提示。
修改 bg_color 签名后, 不要遗漏旧的单参数调用, 否则构造时会出错。
Do not leave 'raise' in the except branch. An exception escaping a Qt slot crashes or silently breaks the command flow instead of informing the user.
Do not call obj.run(argv) after the check fails. The early return is mandatory.
Do not widen the except clause to a bare except or to Exception. Only TypeError from check() means a bad argument count.
Do not move the arg-count validation into Command.run or into individual commands. The check/run split in CommandParser is the single dispatch point.
Do not print or log instead of emitting. User-visible errors go through the error signal.
procedure: Locate CommandParser.parse in qutebrowser/commands.py. Confirm it splits the text and passes the argument list as one positional value, for example obj.check(parts[1:]).

Check Command.check and Command.run for a signature mismatch. If they are declared as *args while callers pass a single list, args becomes a 1-tuple that wraps the list. len(args) is then always 1, so the nargs check is wrong.
Change the signatures to def check(self, argv) and def run(self, argv). Keep one consistent name, argv, across parse, check and run.

Keep the nargs rules in check and apply them to len(argv): an int means an exact count, '?' means at most 1, and '+' means at least 1. Keep raising TypeError('Invalid argument count!') so parse's existing try/except contract stays the same.

In the base Command.run, keep the guard 'if not self.signal: raise NotImplementedError'. The default should emit the signal with no arguments (self.signal.emit()), which suits nargs=0 commands such as QuitCmd.

For each Command subclass whose pyqtSignal has parameters (for example pyqtSignal(str) in OpenCmd and TabOpenCmd), override run(self, argv). Map the elements of argv onto the signal parameters explicitly, for example self.signal.emit(argv[0]).
Review every subclass in cmd_dict. Its nargs, its pyqtSignal signature and the argument count used in its run emit call must all agree.
Define a subclass of Command. Set three class attributes: name (registered in cmd_dict), nargs, and signal = pyqtSignal(...).
If the signal takes no parameters and nargs == 0, rely on the base run, which calls self.signal.emit().
If the signal takes parameters, override run(self, argv) and emit converted values from argv (for example argv[0], or int(argv[0])). Base the conversions on the pyqtSignal types.
For nargs '?', handle an empty argv explicitly in run, for example with a default value.
定位 qutebrowser/commands.py 中 CommandParser.parse 里 cmd_dict[cmd] 的查找, 这是未知命令会抛 KeyError 的位置。
在 CommandParser (QObject) 上增加类级 pyqtSignal(str), 命名为 error。
把 cmd_dict 查找包进 try/except KeyError, 在 except 中 emit 简短消息, 格式如 '{cmd}: no such command', 然后立即 return, 不再执行 check/run。
在 qutebrowser/widgets/statusbar.py 的 StatusBar 上增加槽方法 disp_error(text): 切换为错误配色 (fg white, bg red), 并用 self.lbl.setText('Error: ' + text) 显示文本。
如果配色工具 bg_color 只接受单个颜色, 把它改为 bg_color(fg, bg), 并更新所有已有调用 (例如 __init__ 中改为 bg_color('white', 'black')), 让 stylesheet 能同时设置前景色和背景色。
在 qutebrowser/app.py 的 main() 里, 和其他 connect 放在一起, 增加 cp.error.connect(mw.status.disp_error)。
其他解析失败 (例如 check 中的参数 TypeError) 也复用同一个 error 信号, 不要另建一条通道。
Open qutebrowser/commands.py and find the method in CommandParser that dispatches commands. It looks up the Command object, then calls obj.check(argv), then obj.run(argv).
Find the try/except TypeError block around obj.check(argv). This is where Command.check signals a wrong number of arguments. The placeholder handler is usually '# TODO' followed by a bare 'raise'.
Replace the bare re-raise with a user-facing report on the parser's existing Qt signal: self.error.emit("{}: invalid argument count".format(cmd)). Use the command name variable already in scope.
Add an early 'return' right after the emit so that obj.run(argv) is never reached after a failed check.
Use the existing 'error' pyqtSignal on CommandParser. Do not create a new signal or a new exception type. Its listeners, such as the statusbar, already display the message.
Keep the message format consistent with other CommandParser errors, such as the unknown-command error: '<cmd>: <lowercase description>'.
validation: run existing tests
Parse 'open http://example.com' and confirm check passes and the signal emits the str 'http://example.com', not a list.
Parse 'open' with no argument and 'open a b'. Both should raise TypeError.
Parse 'quit' and confirm a zero-argument emit with no TypeError from PyQt.
Use grep to confirm no remaining '*args' signatures on Command.check or Command.run.

name: qutebrowser-command-file-io-oserror-to-commanderror
negative_constraints: Do not catch a bare `Exception` or use a bare `except:`. Catch only OSError, so real programming errors still surface through the crash handler.
Do not call message.info (or any success message) after the try block unconditionally. It must sit in `else`, otherwise the user sees success after a failure.
Do not swallow the error with just a log entry or message.error followed by return. Use cmdexc.CommandError, which is the repository's standard way to report errors from commands.
Do not drop the original exception text. Include `{}`.format(e) in the message so the user can see the concrete cause (path or permissions).
Do not pull mainframe.toHtml()/toPlainText() into the try.
procedure: Find the command method (@cmdutils.register) in qutebrowser/browser/commands.py, for example CommandDispatcher.dump_page. Look for the unguarded `with open(dest, ...)` / `f.write(...)` block.
Keep data preparation outside the try block, such as mainframe.toPlainText() / toHtml(). Only file I/O goes inside the try, so the catch does not hide errors from unrelated logic.
Wrap only the open+write in `try:`. Catch `except OSError as e:`. This covers PermissionError, FileNotFoundError, IsADirectoryError and similar errors.

In the except branch, re-raise as `raise cmdexc.CommandError('Could not write page: {}'.format(e))`. Reuse the existing cmdexc module rather than inventing a new error-reporting path. The command framework turns CommandError into an error message in the status bar.
Move the success notification `message.info(self._win_id, "Dumped page to {}.".format(dest))` into the `else:` branch. Success is then reported only when the write actually succeeded.
Apply the same pattern to any similar file-writing command in the same file, such as downloads or saving sessions. Check whether those paths have the same uncaught OSError.

trigger.task_type: Handle errors in a user-facing command that writes or reads files (e.g. :dump-page)

validation: Run the existing tests: `tox -e py` / `pytest tests/` (at least the parts related to browser/commands).
Manually: `:dump-page /nonexistent_dir/x.html` and `:dump-page /` (a directory) should show the error 'Could not write page: ...' with no crash dialog.
Manually: `:dump-page /tmp/ok.html` should show 'Dumped page to /tmp/ok.html.' and create the file.
Run the repository's linters (flake8/pylint via tox) to make sure the try/except/else structure introduces no warnings.

name: qutebrowser-comment-grammar-fix
negative_constraints: Do not change surrounding logic, such as the triggerPageAction or setAttribute calls, while fixing a comment.
Do not rename identifiers or change string literals or user-facing messages unless the task explicitly targets them.
Do not reflow, reformat, or restyle unrelated lines or comments.
Do not add a changelog entry or tests for a comment-only spelling fix.
procedure: Locate the misspelled or ungrammatical text. Use grep, because the reported line number may be stale. In this PR the target was a comment inside the WebView caret/selection toggle logic in qutebrowser/browser/webview.py.
Check that the text is a pure comment or docstring, and not a string literal, identifier, config key, or user-visible message that tests or other code depend on.

Rewrite only the wrong wording into idiomatic English, for example change '# Remove selection if exist' to '# Remove selection if it exists'. Keep the original meaning, indentation, and '# ' comment style.
Grep the repository for the same phrase. Fix other identical occurrences only if they are clearly the same typo and also live in comments.
Keep the diff minimal: change one line per occurrence and leave nearby code untouched.
validation: Check that git diff shows only comment or docstring text changes.
Run the repo's style checks (flake8/pylint) if available, to confirm comment formatting and line length still pass.
Optionally run the existing tests to confirm no behavior change. None is expected.

name: qutebrowser-comment-style-type-annotations-for-empty-containers
negative_constraints: Do not use PEP 526 syntax such as `windows: List[...] = []`. It breaks compatibility with older Python versions and the repository's existing style.
Do not keep a regular explanatory comment on the same line as `# type:`. Mypy can fail to parse it, or the explanation gets lost.
Do not use a vague `typing.List[typing.Any]` or `list` when the element structure can be determined from the appends.
Do not change runtime logic, variable names, or function signatures. This is an annotation-only change.
Do not add a changelog entry or tests for a pure type-annotation change.
procedure: Locate the variables mypy cannot infer. These are typically empty-container initializations like `x = []` or `x = {}`. In this PR they were the `windows` and `tabs` lists in `_buffer()` in miscmodels.py.

Infer the element type from the code that writes to the container. In `_buffer()`, `tabs.append(("{}/{}".format(win_id, idx + 1), url, title))` appends 3-tuples of str. These match the three columns declared by `CompletionModel(column_widths=(6, 40, 54))`, so the element type is `typing.Tuple[str, str, str]`.

Use comment-style annotations, not PEP 526 variable annotations. Keep the existing assignment and append `# type: typing.List[typing.Tuple[str, str, str]]`. The repository still supports older Python versions, and other files use this same style.

If the line already has an explanatory inline comment, move it to its own line above the assignment. The `# type:` comment must be the only trailing comment on that line, for example `# list storing all single-tabbed windows when tabs_are_windows`.

Use the fully qualified `typing.X` form. Check whether the module already has `import typing`. If it does not, add `import typing` to the standard-library import group at the top of the file. Do not use `from typing import ...`.
When several containers hold the same kind of data, give them identical annotations. Here `windows` also receives elements taken from `tabs`, so both use the same type.
validation: Run mypy via tox (e.g. `tox -e mypy`) and confirm the 'Need type annotation' error for the affected variables is gone.
Run the completion-model tests: `pytest tests/unit/completion/test_models.py`.
Run flake8/pylint (`tox -e flake8`, `tox -e pylint`) and confirm there is no unused-import or line-too-long error. Keep lines under 79 characters.
Grep the file to confirm `import typing` exists and every annotation uses the `typing.` prefix.

name: qutebrowser-completion-context-via-completioninfo
negative_constraints: Do not filter with a truthiness check like `if skip_win_id and win_id == skip_win_id`. Window id 0 is falsy, so the first window would never be skipped. Use `skip_win_id is not None`.
Do not read the current window from global state inside the model, such as the last-focused window from objreg. Use the `info.win_id` that the completer passes in.
Do not change the behaviour of `:buffer` completion. It must still list tabs from all windows.
Do not duplicate the tab-listing and delete_buffer logic in a second function. Share it through the private helper.
Do not forget test fixtures and helpers that construct CompletionInfo or Completer positionally or with keywords. Adding the new attr.ib breaks them.
procedure: In completer.py, add a field to the attrs class CompletionInfo, e.g. `win_id = attr.ib()`. This is the only channel that delivers context to completion functions (`func(*args, info=info)`).
Add a `win_id` parameter to `Completer.__init__(self, cmd, win_id, parent=None)` and store it as `self._win_id`. Document it in the Attributes section of the class docstring.
Where Completer builds CompletionInfo before calling the model function, pass `win_id=self._win_id`.
Update the Completer construction site in mainwindow/mainwindow.py so it passes the window's own `self.win_id`. Grep every `Completer(` call, including in tests, and update them all.
In miscmodels.py, wrap the existing model body in a private helper such as `_buffer(skip_win_id=None)`. Inside the window-iteration loop, `continue` past `skip_win_id`.
Keep the public `buffer(*, info=None)` behaviour unchanged by having it call `_buffer()`.
Add the new public model `other_buffer(*, info)`, which returns `_buffer(skip_win_id=info.win_id)`. Make `info` required, because the model cannot work without it.
Apply the same pattern to the window model used by :tab-give: skip `info.win_id` when listing target windows.
In browser/commands.py, switch the decorator to `@cmdutils.argument('index', completion=miscmodels.other_buffer)` for tab_take. Point tab_give's window argument at the window-excluding model.

trigger.task_type: Make a completion model depend on the invoking window (e.g. hide the current window for :tab-give/:tab-take)

validation: Run pytest tests/unit/completion/test_models.py and test_completer.py.
Add a test that other_buffer with info.win_id=0 excludes window 0 tabs but includes window 1 tabs. This catches the falsy-id bug.
Add a test that buffer() still includes all windows.
Add a test that the window completion for tab-give omits the current window.
Update the mainwindow/completer fixtures to pass win_id, then run the full unit suite.
Add a changelog entry under Changed: :tab-give/:tab-take completion no longer shows the current window.

name: qutebrowser-docstring-typo-fix
negative_constraints: 不要在修 typo 时改动类属性 (keystring/error/text) 或任何逻辑代码。
不要重写 docstring 的格式或补充新内容, 例如改成多行或加 Args 段, 只修正拼写。
如果拼错的词是公开标识符或信号名, 不要当作 typo 去重命名, 那属于 API 变更, 需要另行处理。
不要为纯 docstring 修正新增测试或 changelog 条目。
Do not change option names, nargs, dest, or metavar. The tests and qtutils.get_args depend on them.
Do not refactor the argparser structure as part of a lint or typo fix.
procedure: 定位: 用 grep 搜出拼写错误的 token (例如 'composedof') 在 qutebrowser/ 下出现的全部位置, 以确认 typo 的作用范围。
判断: 确认 typo 只出现在 docstring 或注释里 (例如 class StatusText(QLabel) 的类 docstring), 而不在标识符、字符串常量或配置键中。
修改: 只在原位改正 typo 本身, 例如补上缺失的空格, 把 'composedof' 改成 'composed of'。docstring 原有的引号风格和其余措辞都保持不变。
检查同类: 在同一文件 (statusbar.py, 包括 StatusProgress、StatusText 等类) 里顺带扫一眼, 看有没有同一种粘连词。只有在同属文案类修正时才一并改掉。
保持 diff 最小: 每处 typo 对应单行替换, 不连带做重排或重构。
Find get_argparser() in qutebrowser/qutebrowser.py. The debug option group is where options like --qt-arg and --qt-flag are added.
Fix grammar errors in help= strings, for example 'a argument' → 'an argument'. Keep the wording consistent with the sibling options, e.g. 'Pass an argument with a value to Qt.'
After editing, check that the line still fits within the length limit and that the continuation lines stay aligned with the opening parenthesis of add_argument.
validation: git diff 应只包含 docstring 或注释的文本变化, 没有逻辑行变动。
python -m py_compile qutebrowser/widgets/statusbar.py 能通过, 确认引号没有被破坏。
再次 grep 原 typo token, 应无残留。
如果仓库配置了 pylint/flake8, 运行一次, 确认没有引入新的告警。

name: qutebrowser-enable-setting-on-webengine-version-gated
negative_constraints: Do not make backends=None unconditional. On older Qt, QtWebEngine would then expose a setting that has no mapping.
Do not reference QWebEngineSettings.<NewAttr> outside a try/except AttributeError.
Do not leave the attribute in the 'Missing QtWebEngine attributes' comment once it is supported.
Do not forget src2asciidoc. Otherwise the generated docs depend on the build machine's Qt version.
Do not change unrelated options' backend lists or the existing MAPPINGS structure.
procedure: Find the QWebEngineSettings attribute in the 'Missing QtWebEngine attributes' comment list in webenginesettings.py. Note the Qt version that introduced it, for example PrintElementBackgrounds (5.8). Delete that line from the comment list.

At the end of webenginesettings.py, add a block that follows the existing version-gated pattern: try: MAPPINGS['<section>']['<option>'] = Attribute(QWebEngineSettings.<Attr>) except AttributeError: pass. Put a '# Added in Qt X.Y' comment in the except branch.
Do not register the attribute directly in the static MAPPINGS dict literal. Older Qt versions do not have the attribute, and that would raise at import time.
In configdata.py, change the option's SettingValue backends from [usertypes.Backend.QtWebKit] to (None if qtutils.version_check('X.Y') else [usertypes.Backend.QtWebKit]).
Add a line to the option's description string, separated by '\n': 'This setting only works with Qt X.Y or newer when using the QtWebEngine backend.'

In scripts/dev/src2asciidoc.py, add (section, option) to the version_dependent_options list in _generate_setting_section, following the existing ('network', 'proxy') entry. Keep the comparison as membership with 'in'. This stops the docs from saying 'only available with QtWebKit' based on the backends value of the Qt that generated them.
Regenerate or check the asciidoc settings documentation so the description and backend note are consistent.

trigger.task_type: Add support for a previously QtWebKit-only setting with QtWebEngine (Qt-version-dependent)

validation: Run the existing tests, e.g. tox / pytest tests/unit/config and tests/unit/browser/webengine.
Check that the config tests asserting each option's backend mapping consistency pass on both new and old Qt, or that they skip appropriately.
Run scripts/dev/src2asciidoc.py and check that the option's documentation has no 'only available with QtWebKit' note and includes the Qt version sentence.
Run flake8/pylint for the repository's line-length and parenthesized multi-line style.

name: qutebrowser-eventfilter-qkeyevent-cast
negative_constraints: Do not delete or weaken the try/except in eventFilter. An exception escaping it while the filter stays installed causes infinite recursion and a stack overflow.
Do not widen the handler parameters to QEvent and then use isinstance inside the handlers; that changes runtime behaviour.
Do not use a blanket `# type: ignore` on the handler call when cast can narrow the type precisely.
Do not mix typing.X and bare-X styles within one file.
procedure: Locate the generic QEvent dispatch points: EventFilter.eventFilter in qutebrowser/keyinput/eventfilter.py and ModeManager.handle_event in qutebrowser/keyinput/modeman.py. Both pick a handler from a dict keyed by event.type().

Keep the existing runtime guard (event.type() in self._handlers / handlers). Fix only the static types: the handlers really take QKeyEvent, so narrow the parameter type of the handler dict's Callable from QEvent to QKeyEvent (e.g. Mapping[QEvent.Type, Callable[[QKeyEvent], bool]]).

At the call site, narrow with cast(QKeyEvent, event) and do not change the handler signatures to accept QEvent. The cast is valid because KeyPress/KeyRelease/ShortcutOverride events are always QKeyEvent instances.

Follow each module's existing typing import style. eventfilter.py adds `import typing` and uses typing.cast. modeman.py uses the unqualified names Mapping/Callable/cast, so confirm the matching `from typing import ...` exists or add it, and that QKeyEvent is imported from PyQt5.QtGui.
Keep the inline `# type:` comment annotation format; the repository is not converting these to variable annotations at this point.
If the handler dict uses functools.partial (e.g. _handle_keypress with dry_run=True), make sure its signature stays compatible with Callable[[QKeyEvent], bool].
validation: Run mypy via tox (e.g. tox -e mypy) and confirm keyinput/eventfilter.py and keyinput/modeman.py report no errors.
Run the existing tests: pytest tests/unit/keyinput.
Run flake8/pylint to check line length and unused imports (typing, cast, QKeyEvent).

name: qutebrowser-falsy-win-id-sentinel-check
negative_constraints: Do not use truthiness (`if x`, `x or default`) on window ids, tab indices, or counts where 0 is valid.
Do not change the default from None to -1 or similar to work around the bug. Keep None as the 'no skip' sentinel and compare with `is not None`.
Do not alter completion column widths, model structure, or the categories produced. The fix is limited to the filter condition.
Do not fix only the reported call site while leaving identical patterns in the same function family.
procedure: Locate the optional-id parameter that defaults to None (e.g. `_buffer(skip_win_id=None)` in miscmodels.py) and every guard that uses it.
Identify guards written as `if skip_win_id and ...` or `if win_id:`. win_id 0 is a valid id (the first window in objreg.window_registry), so these guards silently disable the skip for window 0.

Replace the truthiness test with an explicit sentinel test: `if skip_win_id is not None and win_id == skip_win_id: continue`. Keep the loop over objreg.window_registry and the `tabbed-browser` lookup unchanged.

Search the same module and its callers (other_buffer / tab_take completion, commands.py tab_take and tab_give) for the same `if <id> and` / `if not <id>` pattern on win_id, tab index, or count values, and apply the same fix where 0 is a legal value.
Add or extend a test in tests/unit/completion/test_models.py. Register windows with ids 0 and 1, request the completion with the skip id set to 0, and assert that window 0's tabs are excluded.
Add a changelog entry under the Fixed section (doc/changelog.asciidoc) describing the user-visible effect, e.g. :tab-take completion now excludes the current window when it is window 0.

trigger.task_type: Fix window/tab id 0 being mishandled by truthiness checks (e.g. :tab-take / :tab-give / buffer completion including or skipping the wrong window)

validation: Run existing tests: pytest tests/unit/completion/test_models.py.
Run a new test with skip_win_id=0 and confirm window 0 is excluded and other windows are present.
Run a regression test with skip_win_id=None and confirm all windows, including 0, are listed.
Manual check: start qutebrowser with a single first window (id 0), open a second window, run :tab-take in window 0, and confirm the completion lists only the other window's tabs.

name: qutebrowser-fix-attribute-defined-outside-init-via-reset
negative_constraints: Do not delete or rename reset(). It is part of the lexer's runtime state cycle.
Do not change default values while inlining them; the defaults in __init__ and reset() must stay identical.
Do not add a class-level `# pylint: disable=attribute-defined-outside-init` as the fix.
Do not add new type annotations that change mypy inference unless lint requires it.
procedure: Find classes whose `__init__` calls `self.reset()` (or a similar helper) and where pylint reports attribute-defined-outside-init for attributes assigned only in that helper. An example is ShellLexer in misc/split.py.

Replace the `self.reset()` call in `__init__` with explicit assignments of every attribute that reset() sets, using the exact same default values. In ShellLexer these are quoted=False, escapedstate=' ', token='' and state=' '.
Keep reset() unchanged, because other callers (e.g. split()) still use it to reinitialise state.
Diff the attributes set in __init__ against those set in reset() and check that nothing is missing and every default matches.
validation: Run pylint on the file and confirm attribute-defined-outside-init is gone.
Run the existing tests, e.g. `pytest tests/unit/misc/test_split.py` (including hypothesis/yaml-driven cases), and confirm tokenisation behavior is unchanged.
Run mypy to confirm attribute types are still inferred consistently.

name: qutebrowser-fix-bool-to-enum-config-migration
negative_constraints: Do not swap or guess the positional true/false arguments without reading the _migrate_bool signature.
Do not map old False to a value that changes user-visible behavior more than necessary. Pick the new default or closest equivalent, not an extreme like 'never' if that was not the old behavior.
Do not add a separate custom migration function when the _migrate_bool helper fits.
Do not modify migration entries for unrelated settings.
Do not omit the pass-through test case for values that are already migrated strings.
procedure: Locate the migration call for the setting in YamlConfig's migration handling in qutebrowser/config/configfiles.py. The call has the form self._migrate_bool(settings, name, true_value, false_value).
Confirm the argument order from the helper's signature: the third argument is the value for True and the fourth is the value for False.

Derive the correct mapping from the old setting's semantics, not from the new default. Old True must map to the closest equivalent of 'shown', and old False to the closest equivalent of 'hidden'. For scrolling.bar: True becomes 'always' and False becomes 'when-searching', the default that replaced 'off'.
Check that both target values are valid options of the new enum in configdata.yml.
Change only the true_value/false_value literals in the existing _migrate_bool call. Reuse the helper instead of hand-writing a conversion.

Add parametrized cases in tests/unit/config/test_configfiles.py next to the other migrate_bool cases (the tabs.favicons.show and qt.force_software_rendering blocks). Include three tuples: (name, True, expected_true), (name, False, expected_false), and (name, already_valid_string, same_string) to show that non-bool values pass through unchanged.
validation: Run pytest tests/unit/config/test_configfiles.py -k migrate.
Run pytest tests/unit/config/test_configfiles.py.
Manually load an autoconfig.yml containing the setting with value true and then false, and verify the migrated values after load.

name: qutebrowser-flags-with-args-literal-flag-matching
negative_constraints: 不要在 flags_with_args 里存 param.name，再在消费端用 lstrip('-') 或 replace('-', '_') 做近似匹配。登记和查询必须使用同一种表示：命令行字面量 flag。
不要只登记 long_flag 或只登记 short_flag。两种写法用户都会输入，都会影响 flag_arg_count。
不要把 bool 类型的 flag 加入 flags_with_args。它们不消耗后续参数，加入会让 maxsplit 偏移过多。
不要改动 maxsplit 的计算公式（i + cmd.maxsplit + flag_arg_count）来掩盖匹配问题。根因在键空间不一致。
procedure: 先定位登记点。在 command.py 的 Command 参数注册逻辑中，找到生成 long_flag/short_flag 并写入 self.opt_args 的分支。该分支里 `typ is not bool` 时会把参数登记到 self.flags_with_args。
再定位消费点。在 runners.py 的 CommandRunner 中，找到按 maxsplit 切分参数的循环。循环里对以 '-' 开头的 arg 查 cmd.flags_with_args，并据此递增 flag_arg_count。
核对两端的键空间。登记端如果存的是 param.name（Python 名，下划线形式，且和短 flag 字母无关），消费端却用 arg.lstrip('-') 去匹配，那么短 flag（如 -s）和含连字符的长 flag（如 --some-flag）都匹配不上。结果是 flag_arg_count 漏加，maxsplit 位置算错，flag 的值被当成位置参数吞掉。
修复登记端。改为登记命令行上真实出现的字面量：`self.flags_with_args += [short_flag, long_flag]`，直接复用 argparse 注册时已经算好的 short_flag 和 long_flag，不要另行推导。
修复消费端。改为对 strip 后的原始 arg 精确匹配：`if arg in cmd.flags_with_args`，不再剥离 '-'。
检查其他读者。全仓搜索 flags_with_args 的读取方，确认没有调用方仍假设其元素是 param.name。如果有，一并迁移到字面量 flag 语义。
补充回归测试，覆盖带 maxsplit 的命令：短 flag 带值、长 flag 带值、含下划线的参数名对应的连字符长 flag 带值。断言 flag 的值没有被并入剩余的 maxsplit 文本。

trigger.task_type: Fix handling of flags with args with maxsplit

validation: 运行已有测试：pytest tests/unit/commands。
新增或确认用例：一个 maxsplit=0 且带非 bool flag 的命令。分别用 '-x val rest of text' 和 '--long-name val rest of text' 调用，断言 flag 值为 'val'，位置参数为 'rest of text'。
确认 bool flag 与 maxsplit 组合的行为保持不变。

name: qutebrowser-get-qt-args-prefix-filter
negative_constraints: Do not handle non-Qt arguments with a `pass` that has no effect. An argparse filter loop must use `continue` to skip them.
Do not rewrite how qt_ argument names are converted (prefix stripping, '-' prefix) or how values are serialized, unless the task asks for it.
Do not drop or reorder the leading sys.argv[0] in argv.
Do not test only with all-qt_ or all-None namespaces. That covers the happy path and misses this bug.
procedure: Locate get_qt_args(namespace) in qutebrowser/utils/misc.py. It iterates over vars(namespace).items() and turns every argument that starts with qt_ into a Qt argv entry: a flag becomes '-name', a value becomes '-name value'.

Check the prefix filter. If it is written as `if not argname.startswith('qt_'): pass`, that `pass` is a no-op. Non-qt_ arguments then fall through to the None/True/value branches, and qutebrowser's own options leak into the Qt argv.
Change `pass` to `continue`, so every argument without the qt_ prefix is skipped.
Turn the following `if val is None` into `elif val is None`, so the filter, None, True and value checks form one mutually exclusive if/elif chain.

Leave the existing qt_ handling logic unchanged: argv starts with sys.argv[0], None means not given, True means a bare flag, other values become a flag plus a value. The minimal fix touches only the control flow.

Add or extend a unit test in tests/unit/utils/test_misc.py. Build an argparse.Namespace that has both qt_* and non-qt_* attributes, some set to True or a string. Assert that the returned argv contains only sys.argv[0] plus the arguments derived from qt_*.
validation: Run the existing tests: pytest tests/unit/utils/test_misc.py -k qt_args
New regression case: a Namespace with a non-qt_ arg set to True or a string (e.g. debug=True, url='x') must not appear in the result.
Confirm that combinations of qt_ flags (True) and qt_ values (strings) still produce argv in the original format.

name: qutebrowser-import-grouping-third-party
negative_constraints: Do not treat pkg_resources (setuptools), attr, or pytest as standard library.
Do not change any logic or rename anything while fixing lint. Only move imports and adjust whitespace.
Do not reorder all imports alphabetically across groups and break the three-group structure.
procedure: Locate the import block of the file the lint complains about, and of any related test file that imports the same module (for example, the tests/unit/utils/test_version.py that corresponds to qutebrowser/utils/version.py).

Sort imports into three groups: (1) stdlib, such as os, sys, subprocess, importlib, collections, enum, datetime; (2) third-party, such as attr, pkg_resources, pytest, PyQt5; (3) qutebrowser's own modules. Separate the groups with one blank line.

Move any third-party module that sits in the stdlib group into the third-party group. pkg_resources belongs to setuptools, so it is third-party. Within the group, follow the existing order, for example attr, then pkg_resources, then pytest or PyQt5.
Apply the same move to the paired test file in the same change, so source and tests are not left with different import groupings.
validation: Run pylint or flake8 on the changed files (for example, `tox -e pylint` or `tox -e flake8`) and confirm the import-order warnings are gone.
Run the existing tests: `pytest tests/unit/utils/test_version.py`.

name: qutebrowser-key-configtype-post-parse-validation
negative_constraints: 不要把校验放进 keyutils.KeySequence.parse,也不要放进 keyparser 或 bind 命令里。那样会影响非配置场景的按键解析,还会漏掉某些配置入口。
不要禁止 Qt.Key_0。0 可以作为普通绑定(例如 scroll 到行首),count 只从 1-9 起始。
不要禁止带修饰键的数字,例如 <alt-1> 用于 tab-focus。检查条件里必须带 not info.modifiers。
不要只检查序列的第一个键。'a1' 这类序列中间出现的数字同样要拒绝。
不要抛出 KeyParseError 或其他异常类型。配置层只认 configexc.ValidationError。
不要用字符串匹配(如 value.isdigit())代替 KeyInfo 判断。'<1>' 这类写法会绕过字符串检查。

name: qutebrowser-keyinfo-to-qkeyevent-helper

name: qutebrowser-keyparser-drop-speculative-fixme
negative_constraints: Do not implement the suggestion in the FIXME, such as rewriting key matching with QKeySequence.matches, as part of a Remove FIXME task.
Do not change the logging format string, the key/text extraction, or the early-return branch for empty text.
Do not convert the FIXME into a TODO or an issue reference unless asked.

procedure: In qutebrowser/utils/keyparser.py, find the FIXME comment inside the KeyParser key-handling method (the one whose docstring says 'e: the KeyPressEvent from Qt').

negative_constraints: 不要顺手实现 QKeySequence 重构。本任务只加注释，不改任何逻辑、日志或返回值。

name: qutebrowser-keyparser-type-annotations
negative_constraints: 不要改变任何运行时行为、匹配逻辑或信号定义,只增加类型信息。
不要保留 `MYPY = False` 守卫并与 `import typing` 混用,导入风格要保持一致。
不要用 `typing.Any` 糊弄能确定的类型,例如匹配结果元组要写清结构。
不要把私有类型别名暴露为公共名称,保持 `_` 前缀。
不要顺带修改其他 keyinput 模块的签名,除非 mypy 因此报错。
procedure: 定位 qutebrowser/keyinput/basekeyparser.py 中的 `MYPY = False` / `if MYPY:` 条件导入块。删除这个块,改成在模块顶部无条件 `import typing`。之后统一写成 `typing.Optional`、`typing.Mapping`、`typing.MutableMapping` 这种带模块前缀的形式。

把重复出现的复合返回类型提取为模块级私有别名,放在 imports 之后。例如 `_MatchType = typing.Tuple[QKeySequence.SequenceMatch, typing.Optional[str]]`。对 `_match_without_modifiers` / `_match_key_mapping` 这类同时返回序列的方法,另外定义 `_MatchSequenceType`,在元组末尾追加 `keyutils.KeySequence`。
给注解中用到的 Qt 类型补上真实导入,例如 `from PyQt5.QtGui import QKeySequence, QKeyEvent`、`from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QWidget`。不要使用字符串前向引用或 TYPE_CHECKING 守卫。
所有方法都显式标注返回类型。`__init__`、`__setitem__`、`_debug_log` 这类无返回值的方法写 `-> None`。`__repr__` 写 `-> str`。`matches` / `_match_key` 写 `-> _MatchType`。`__getitem__` 写 `-> typing.Optional[str]`。
给参数补具体类型。例如 `win_id: int`、`parent: QWidget = None`、`supports_count: bool = True`、`sequence: keyutils.KeySequence`、`message: str`、`e: QKeyEvent`。
实例属性沿用 `# type:` 注释风格,例如 `self.child = {}  # type: typing.MutableMapping[keyutils.KeyInfo, BindingTrie]`。行宽超过 79 时,把字面量拆到下一行,保持类型注释在闭合括号所在行。
签名过长时,在参数之间换行并与左括号对齐,确保满足 flake8/pylint 行宽限制。

name: qutebrowser-keyparser-unconditional-escape-reset
negative_constraints: 不要把重置逻辑放在 handled/_supports_chains 提前返回之后,否则已绑定的 <Esc> 会跳过重置。
不要在重置后直接 return Match.none 或 True/False,否则会吞掉 <Esc> 绑定的命令执行或改变 handled 语义。
不要只清空 self._keystring 而不 emit keystring_updated,否则 UI 会显示陈旧的按键序列。
不要在 _handle_single_key 中保留重复的 Escape 处理分支。
不要捕获宽泛的 Exception, 只捕获 KeyParseError。
不要在 dry_run 之外引入新的副作用或弹出用户可见的错误消息; 只做 debug 日志。
不要绕过 _match_key/key_mappings 逻辑去重新实现匹配。
procedure: 定位 BaseKeyParser.handle(e): 它先调用 _handle_special_key(e),并且会在 `if handled or not self._supports_chains: return handled` 处提前返回。再定位 _handle_single_key 中现有的 `if key == Qt.Key_Escape` 早返回分支。
删除 _handle_single_key 里的 Escape 分支。该分支只在特殊键未处理且解析器支持 chains 时才会执行,所以当 <Esc> 已被绑定(作为特殊键被处理)时,keystring 不会被重置。
在 handle() 中,紧跟在 `handled = self._handle_special_key(e)` 之后、`if handled or not self._supports_chains` 提前返回之前,加入无条件检查 `if e.key() == Qt.Key_Escape:`。这样不论 <Esc> 是否被绑定,都会执行清理。
在该分支中复用 self._debug_log 记录被丢弃的 keystring,然后设置 self._keystring = '',并发出 self.keystring_updated.emit(self._keystring),让状态栏等监听者感知清空。
不要在 Escape 分支里 return。保留 handled 的值和后续流程,使已绑定的 <Esc> 命令(例如离开模式)照常执行。
在分支上方加注释链接 issue #716,说明这是特意保留的特殊情况。
当 Qt 送来的 key 事件可能导致 keyutils 构造序列失败时, 将失败统一表达为 keyutils.KeyParseError。
在 BaseKeyParser.handle 唯一的序列扩展点 (append_event) 捕获该异常; count 处理分支保持不变。
失败时执行三步: debug log (包含异常文本)、clear_keystring() (同时重置 count 和 sequence, 并发出 keystring_updated)、return QKeySequence.NoMatch, 使上层 modeman 将事件视为未处理。
为该路径编写回归测试: 先建立部分 keychain, 再注入非法事件, 断言状态已清空。

name: qutebrowser-keyseq-validate-raise-not-assert
negative_constraints: 不要用 assert 校验来自用户配置或命令行的 keystring。assert 会产生 AssertionError(crash),或在 -O 下被跳过。
不要只特判 Qt.Key_unknown 而放行越界值; 必须同时检查下界(Key_Space)和上界。
不要在测试中保留期望 AssertionError 的用例。
不要在 parse 的调用方吞掉 KeyParseError 之外的异常来掩盖问题。
procedure: 定位 qutebrowser/keyinput/keyutils.py 中的 KeySequence._validate 及其他由 parse/__init__ 调用的校验路径。逐一检查对用户输入(keystring、key code)做 assert 的位置。

对空子序列(例如 '<>' 解析后得到的空 seq)同样抛出 KeyParseError, 不要用 assert。
错误信息保持统一, 例如 'Got invalid key!'。复用已有的 KeyParseError 签名, 第一个参数传 keystr。

在 test_parse 的参数表中加入触发新路径的输入, 例如 '<>'。
增加 hypothesis 模糊测试: 用 @hypothesis.given(strategies.text()) 调用 KeySequence.parse。解析成功时调用 str(seq), 确保渲染不崩溃; 抛出 KeyParseError 时视为合法结果。

name: qutebrowser-keysequence-chunked-matching
negative_constraints: Do not finish with an unconditional ExactMatch after zip(). zip stops silently at the shorter list, so a configured binding with more chunks would wrongly report ExactMatch instead of PartialMatch.
Do not swap the roles of self and other. The direction of the match decides PartialMatch versus NoMatch.
Do not flatten to the raw Qt key list or reimplement Qt's prefix matching. Delegate per-chunk matching to QKeySequence.matches.
Do not keep asserts that reject empty _sequences. The keyparser can call matches with empty input.
Do not test only bindings of 4 keys or fewer. The bug only appears when a binding spans more than one QKeySequence chunk.
procedure: Locate KeySequence.matches in qutebrowser/keyinput/keyutils.py. Remember that a KeySequence stores keys in self._sequences, a list of QKeySequence chunks with at most 4 keys each. Comparing two KeySequences therefore means comparing chunk by chunk, and the two sides can have a different number of chunks.
Treat self as the keys the user entered and other as the configured binding. Use those names, entered and configured, in the loop and in comments so the asymmetry is visible.
Return QKeySequence.NoMatch early when len(self._sequences) > len(other._sequences). If the user entered more chunks than the binding has, it can never match.

Zip the two chunk lists. For each pair, call entered.matches(configured), which reuses Qt's per-chunk QKeySequence.matches. If the result is not ExactMatch, return it immediately, because a NoMatch or PartialMatch in any chunk decides the outcome.

Once every shared chunk is an ExactMatch, decide by chunk count. Equal counts return ExactMatch. Fewer entered chunks than configured return PartialMatch, since more keypresses could still complete the binding. The remaining case cannot happen, so guard it with an assert that includes (self, other).

Remove the old `assert self._sequences` and `assert other._sequences` so that empty sequences are allowed. With the new logic, empty vs empty gives ExactMatch, empty vs a binding gives PartialMatch, and a binding vs empty gives NoMatch.
Add a parametrized test_matches(entered, configured, expected) to TestKeySequence. Build both sides with KeySequence.parse and import QKeySequence from PyQt5.QtGui.
In the tests, cover cases inside a single chunk ('abc'/'abcd' gives Partial, 'abcd'/'abcd' gives Exact, 'ax'/'abcd' gives NoMatch).
Cover the boundary across chunks ('abcd'/'abcdef' and 'abcde'/'abcdef' give Partial, 'abcdx'/'abcdef' gives NoMatch, 'abcdef'/'abcdef' gives Exact).
Cover the case where entered is longer than configured ('abcdef'/'abcd', 'abcdefg'/'abcdef' and 'ab'/'a' give NoMatch).
Cover the three empty-string cases listed above.
validation: Run pytest tests/unit/keyinput/test_keyutils.py -k matches.
Run the full tests/unit/keyinput suite to confirm the keyparser and BaseKeyParser binding resolution still pass.
Manually check that a binding longer than 4 keys gives PartialMatch at 4 and 5 keys typed, and ExactMatch once fully typed.
Run pylint on keyutils.py and keep the protected-access disable for other._sequences.

name: qutebrowser-keysequence-explicit-int-conversion
negative_constraints: Do not let the constructor accept str implicitly. String input must go through KeySequence.parse.
Do not remove or weaken self._validate() or the 'assert self' check after converting.
Do not change the _MAX_LEN chunking behavior.
Do not convert keys with a silent try/except fallback. Use an explicit assert so misuse surfaces in tests.
procedure: Locate the place in KeySequence.__init__ in qutebrowser/keyinput/keyutils.py where each chunk produced by utils.chunk(keys, self._MAX_LEN) is passed straight into QKeySequence(*sub).

Add a private method _convert_key(self, key). It first asserts isinstance(key, (int, Qt.KeyboardModifiers)), passing the key as the assert message. It then returns int(key). This keeps the conversion and type check in one place.
In __init__, build args = [self._convert_key(key) for key in sub] and call QKeySequence(*args). Leave the chunking, the 'if keys: assert self' check and the trailing self._validate() call unchanged.

Search tests/unit/keyinput/test_keyutils.py and other callers for code that passes str values to the KeySequence(...) constructor, for example KeySequence('b') or the '\x1f' entry in test_init_unknown. Rewrite each to use KeySequence.parse('...'). For an invalid-string case, split it into its own test that expects keyutils.KeyParseError from KeySequence.parse.
Keep the int-based invalid inputs (Qt.Key_unknown, -1, 0) in test_init_unknown. They must still raise KeyParseError through _validate.

name: qutebrowser-keyutils-qt-int-type-annotations
negative_constraints: Do not annotate values that may carry modifier bits as Qt.Key. That gives a false sense of type safety and causes mypy errors.
Do not change runtime logic or the assertion semantics. This change is annotation-only, apart from equivalent literal replacements such as Qt.Key(0).
Do not drop _assert_plain_key/_assert_plain_modifier because annotations are now present. The annotations cannot express the 'no modifiers mixed in' constraint.
Do not use `from typing import ...` or other styles that conflict with the existing code.
procedure: Locate the unannotated functions in qutebrowser/keyinput/keyutils.py: _build_special_names, _assert_plain_key, _assert_plain_modifier, _is_printable, is_special(_hint_mode), is_modifier_key, _is_surrogate, _remap_unicode, _check_valid_utf8, and the rest of the module.
Type parameters that hold a key value (from QKeyEvent::key(), possibly ORed with modifiers) as `int`, not `Qt.Key`, because Qt actually returns an int.
Type modifier parameters as `Qt.KeyboardModifier`. At function entry, keep or reuse the runtime assertions _assert_plain_key() and _assert_plain_modifier() to guarantee the semantics.
Annotate return values explicitly. Predicates return `-> bool`. Assertion-style helpers return `-> None`. _remap_unicode returns `-> int`. Builder functions return `typing.Mapping[Qt.Key, str]`.
Make dict-literal keys match the annotation. For example, change `{0x0: 'nil'}` to `{Qt.Key(0): 'nil'}` so mypy does not infer Dict[int, str].
Explain in the module docstring why most annotations use int instead of Qt.Key (Qt's lack of type safety, keys mixed with modifiers by OR), so later maintainers do not 'fix' them back by mistake.
Annotate in the existing style: use `import typing` with `typing.X`, and keep the existing import style unchanged.

name: qutebrowser-lint-cleanup-after-per-domain-settings-refactor
negative_constraints: Don't change behavior: no reordering of conditions, no new short-circuiting, and no change to when lambda default args capture values. `url=self._reload_url` must stay bound at definition time.
Don't add `# noqa` or `# pylint: disable` to silence an unused import or a long line that can be fixed for real.
Don't use backslash line continuations; qutebrowser style prefers parentheses.
Don't remove an import that is only used in type comments, in `__all__`, or as a re-export without checking those usages first.
Don't expand the scope to refactoring unrelated code, adding tests, or editing the changelog for a pure lint fix.
procedure: Locate: run tox -e flake8 and tox -e pylint, or use the CI lint output. Start with the modules touched by the most recent feature refactor. In this PR that was the per-URL settings work, which touched webengine/webkit settings and webenginetab.

Remove unused imports: for each module in a grouped import such as `from qutebrowser.config import config, websettings, configutils`, grep the file for `<module>.` usages. Delete only the names with no usages and keep the rest of the import line unchanged.
Check symmetric backends: when a lint error appears in a webengine module, check the matching webkit module (webenginesettings ↔ webkitsettings). The same leftover import often exists in both.

Fix long lines (79-column limit) by extracting a well-named local variable first. Examples: `js_enabled = self.settings.test_attribute(...)` and `needs_reload = {...}` for set literals inside conditions. This keeps the logic unchanged and makes it easier to read.

If a line is still too long, wrap it inside the call parentheses using visual alignment, for example after a lambda's `:` aligned with the opening paren. Use 8-space hanging indent for continuation lines of multi-line `if (...)` conditions so they are visually distinct from the body.
Leave WORKAROUND comments (e.g. QTBUG-66656) and statement order exactly in place. A blank line between logically separate if-blocks is acceptable.
validation: tox -e flake8 (or flake8 on changed files) reports no F401/E501 on the touched files.
tox -e pylint reports no unused-import or line-too-long on the touched files.
Run the existing unit tests for the touched areas, e.g. pytest tests/unit/browser and tests/unit/config, to confirm imports still resolve.
Diff review: every change is an import removal, a local-variable extraction, or whitespace and wrapping only.

name: qutebrowser-logfilter-level-and-wiring-fix
negative_constraints: Do not pass plain lists, strings, or other non-Filter objects to Handler.addFilter.
Do not invert the level check so that DEBUG bypasses the filter. --logfilter exists to narrow noisy debug output, and messages more important than DEBUG must never be suppressed.
Do not edit old tests just to make them pass against the buggy semantics. Rewrite the assertions to express the intended behavior.
Do not change name prefix matching or the None-means-all behavior when fixing the level bug.
procedure: In qutebrowser/utils/log.py, find the --logfilter wiring in init_log(). handler.addFilter() must receive a logging.Filter instance, for example console.addFilter(LogFilter(args.logfilter.split(','))). Passing a raw list is wrong: logging treats any object without a .filter method as a callable, and calling a list raises TypeError.

Check the level comparison in LogFilter.filter(). Only DEBUG-level records (record.levelno <= logging.DEBUG) should be filtered by name. Records more important than DEBUG (record.levelno > logging.DEBUG) must return True early. Make sure the comment matches what the condition actually does.

Keep the existing name-matching semantics. A record passes when record.name equals a listed name, or when it starts with that name followed by '.', so child loggers also pass. When self.names is None, every record passes.
Keep the existing activation guard: the filter is only installed when args.logfilter is not None and numeric_level <= logging.DEBUG.

Update LogFilterTests.test_debug in qutebrowser/test/utils/test_log.py. A DEBUG record with a listed name must pass. A DEBUG record with an unlisted name must be filtered. An INFO record must pass whether or not its name is listed. Fix the test docstring so it matches this behavior.
validation: Run the existing tests in qutebrowser/test/utils/test_log.py, especially LogFilterTests.
Manually run init_log with --loglevel debug --logfilter some.name and confirm no TypeError on the first log call.
Confirm that DEBUG records from unlisted loggers are dropped while WARNING and INFO records from them still appear.

name: qutebrowser-mode-enum-names-in-error-messages
negative_constraints: Do not convert self.modes or not_modes to strings at registration or in the decorator. The mode comparison needs enum members (curmode in self.modes).
Do not use str(mode). It gives 'KeyMode.insert' rather than 'insert'.
Do not change the PrerequisitesError type or the message wording. Callers and tests may match on them.
Do not fix only one of the two branches.
procedure: In qutebrowser/commands/command.py, find Command._check_prerequisites (or the equivalent check). It compares modeman.mode against self.modes or self.not_modes.
Confirm that self.modes and self.not_modes hold usertypes.KeyMode enum members, not strings. '/'.join() on them raises TypeError, so the user gets a crash instead of a readable message.
In each branch, build the display string with a generator over the enum names: mode_names = '/'.join(mode.name for mode in self.modes). Use self.not_modes in the not_modes branch.
Pass mode_names into the existing PrerequisitesError format string. Keep the message wording as is: '{name}: This command is only allowed in {modes} mode.' and '... is not allowed in ... mode.'
Fix both branches (modes and not_modes). They share the same defect.

Grep the repo for other '/'.join, ', '.join or str.format calls that take KeyMode or other enum collections, such as the command docs generator or completion. Apply the same .name mapping wherever such a collection is formatted for users.

trigger.task_type: Fix error message when executing command in wrong mode.

validation: Run the existing test suite (tox / pytest tests/).

Add or extend a unit test: create a Command restricted with modes=[KeyMode.insert], set the mode manager to normal, then assert that PrerequisitesError is raised and that its message contains 'insert' and no 'KeyMode'.
Do the same for not_modes.
Manual check: run a mode-restricted command such as :open-editor or a hint command in the wrong mode. It should show the error message in the statusbar, with no traceback.

name: qutebrowser-model-raises-domain-error-command-translates
negative_constraints: 不要在 urlmarks 这类数据/管理层直接抛 cmdexc.CommandError。命令错误只在 commands.py 的命令层抛出。
不要在调用方用宽泛的 except Exception 或 except urlmarks.Error 吞掉异常。只捕获具体的 DoesNotExistError。
不要修改用户可见的错误消息文本,否则会破坏现有测试或用户预期。
不要遗漏任何调用方。漏掉的调用方会让未转换的 DoesNotExistError 冒泡,变成崩溃而不是错误消息。
不要在 cmdexc 仍被同模块其他代码引用时删除它的导入。
procedure: 定位 model/manager 层 (如 qutebrowser/browser/urlmarks.py 中的 QuickmarkManager/UrlMarkManager) 里直接 raise cmdexc.CommandError 的方法 (例如 get_by_qurl)。
复用该模块已定义的领域异常 (urlmarks.DoesNotExistError, 它是 Error 的子类)。只有在没有合适异常时才在模块内新增 Error 子类。
把 raise cmdexc.CommandError(msg) 改为 raise DoesNotExistError(msg)。用户可见的消息文本保持不变,例如 "Quickmark for '{}' not found!"。
检查该模块里 cmdexc 是否还有其他用途。如果没有,就从 'from qutebrowser.commands import cmdexc, cmdutils' 中删掉 cmdexc,只保留 cmdutils 等仍在使用的导入。

grep 被改方法的所有调用方,例如 grep -rn 'get_by_qurl' qutebrowser/。在 qutebrowser/browser/commands.py 的 CommandDispatcher 命令方法 (如 quickmark_del) 中,用 try/except urlmarks.DoesNotExistError as e: raise cmdexc.CommandError(str(e)) 包裹调用,把领域异常转换回命令错误。
确认调用方已 import urlmarks,并且 except 块里的转换使用 str(e) 来保留原消息。

trigger.task_type: Use DoesNotExistError rather than CommandError in get_by_qurl

validation: 运行 grep -rn 'cmdexc' qutebrowser/browser/urlmarks.py,确认已无残留引用,或残留引用确实是必要的。
运行 grep -rn 'get_by_qurl' 列出所有调用方,逐一确认已处理 DoesNotExistError。
运行 pytest tests/ -k 'urlmark or quickmark',以及相关的 BDD 测试 (tests/end2end/features/urlmarks.feature)。
手动验证:在当前页面没有 quickmark 时执行 :quickmark-del,应显示错误消息 "Quickmark for '...' not found!",而不是 traceback。
运行 flake8 或 pylint,确认没有未使用的 import (unused-import)。

name: qutebrowser-move-gl-workaround-before-opengl-probing
negative_constraints: 不要保留两处调用。CDLL 加载虽然幂等,但重复代码会掩盖真实的执行顺序。
不要把 workaround 放在任何会创建 GL 上下文或查询 OpenGL vendor 的代码之后。
不要在 QtWebKit 分支调用。函数内的 backend 断言就是为了限定只用于 QtWebEngine。
不要去掉 utils.is_linux 守卫。在非 Linux 平台上 find_library('GL') 可能返回 None。
不要在 webenginesettings.py 里留下未使用的 ctypes import(flake8/pylint 会报错)。
procedure: 定位那段过晚执行的进程级 workaround。本例是 webenginesettings.init() 里的 ctypes.CDLL(find_library('GL'), RTLD_GLOBAL)。确认它晚于 backendproblem.init() 中的 OpenGL 探测(例如 _handle_nouveau_graphics 会调用 version.opengl_vendor())。
在 qutebrowser/misc/backendproblem.py 中新增私有函数 _nvidia_shader_workaround()。docstring 写明原因、上游 bug 链接,以及顺序约束:必须在 _handle_nouveau_graphics 之前调用,否则 opengl_vendor() 会 segfault。
沿用该模块已有的约定:函数开头写 assert objects.backend == usertypes.Backend.QtWebEngine, objects.backend,并用 utils.is_linux 守卫平台。
在 backendproblem.py 中补齐 import:ctypes、ctypes.util,并把 utils 加入 qutebrowser.utils 的导入。
在 backendproblem.init() 的 QtWebEngine 分支中,把调用插在 _handle_wayland() 之后、_handle_nouveau_graphics() 之前。
从 webenginesettings.init() 删除原有 workaround 代码块,并删掉由此不再使用的 ctypes/ctypes.util import,避免 workaround 被重复执行。
validation: 运行 pytest tests/unit/misc 以及与 webenginesettings 相关的单元测试
运行 flake8/pylint,确认没有未使用或缺失的 import
手动检查 backendproblem.init() 中的调用顺序:_handle_ssl_support -> _handle_wayland -> _nvidia_shader_workaround -> _handle_nouveau_graphics
如有条件,在 Linux 加 Nvidia/nouveau 的环境下启动 qutebrowser --backend webengine,确认不会 segfault

name: qutebrowser-mypy-qflags-cast-or-ignore
negative_constraints: Do not change runtime behaviour: no int() conversions, no reordering of flag operands, no different flag values.
Do not add a blanket `# type: ignore` at file level or on unrelated lines.
Do not rewrite PyQt imports or add stub files in this task. Keep the fix local to the call sites.
Do not cast to a guessed type name that is missing from PyQt5-stubs. Use `# type: ignore` instead.
Do not add tests or changelog entries for typing-only changes.
procedure: Run mypy with the repo config (tox -e mypy). Collect every error where a Qt enum value is combined with `|` and passed to a setter that expects a QFlags type. Typical setters are setWindowFlags, setWindowState, setFlags, QUrl.adjusted and setAlignment.

Decide which fix to use. If the QFlags target type has a stub-visible name such as Qt.WindowFlags or QUrl.FormattingOptions, prefer wrapping the whole OR expression in `typing.cast(<QFlagsType>, a | b | c)`.

Use a `# type: ignore` only on the exact line mypy reports when the stubs cannot express the type, e.g. Qt.WindowFullScreen | self.windowState() or QWebEngineUrlScheme flags. Do not put it on the whole statement.

Multi-line expressions report the error on a specific physical line, which may be the first operand line. Put the ignore on that line. If mypy reports more than one line, add an ignore to each one, as the PR did in mainwindow.setWindowState.
When you add typing.cast, check whether the module already imports `typing`. If it does not, add `import typing` to the stdlib import block, matching the existing import order (see webpage.py).

For flags accumulated with `|=` into a local variable (e.g. window_flags), cast at the call site: `self.setWindowFlags(typing.cast(Qt.WindowFlags, window_flags))`. Do not change how the variable is built.
Apply the same pattern in the utils helpers (debug.py, qtutils.py) that take or return QEnum/QFlags. Add casts there so callers get correct types.
Rerun mypy. If mypy is configured to warn about unused ignores, remove any ignore it reports as unused.

trigger.task_type: mypy: Add ignores/casts for some QEnum/QFlags

validation: Run tox -e mypy (or mypy qutebrowser) and confirm the QFlags/QEnum errors are gone with no new or unused-ignore errors.
Run flake8/pylint (tox -e flake8,pylint) to check line length and import order after rewrapping lines.
Run the existing unit tests for the touched modules (pytest tests/unit/utils tests/unit/mainwindow) to confirm behaviour is unchanged.

name: qutebrowser-narrow-keyutils-public-api
negative_constraints: Do not keep the old public name as a compatibility alias. The goal is to shrink the public surface.
Do not overlook scripts/keytester.py. It is outside the package but still imports keyutils.
Do not carry over `is None` comparisons against a str-returning API. They become dead conditions that are always False.
Do not leave monkeypatch.setattr pointing at a name that no longer exists. With raising=True the test fails; otherwise it silently stops testing anything.
Do not change KeyInfo.__str__ formatting while doing this refactor.
procedure: Grep the whole repository for each public keyutils function: qutebrowser/, scripts/ and tests/. Classify each one as either 'used only inside keyutils' or 'used by external callers'.

For helpers used only inside keyutils.py (for example key_to_string and normalize_keystr), add a '_' prefix to the name. Also update every internal call site in the same module, such as _parse_keystring and KeyInfo.__str__.

For thin wrappers that external callers use, move the logic onto the data class. For example, replace keyevent_to_string(e) with @classmethod KeyInfo.from_event(cls, e) that returns cls(e.key(), e.modifiers()). Then delete the module-level wrapper.
Rewrite the external call sites to str(keyutils.KeyInfo.from_event(e)). This covers basekeyparser.BaseKeyParser.handle (the debug txt), modeparsers.RegisterKeyParser and scripts/keytester.py.
At every call site, check the old return-value semantics. Old checks like `is None` must become falsiness checks such as `not str(...)`, because __str__ always returns str and never None.

Update monkeypatch targets in tests that reference the removed or renamed names. In test_basekeyparser, test_no_binding monkeypatched keyutils.keyevent_to_string. Patch KeyInfo.__str__/from_event instead, or drive the behaviour with a real fake_keyevent.
Rename test functions or parametrizations that test the private helpers directly so they call keyutils._key_to_string and keyutils._normalize_keystr. Alternatively, test them through KeyInfo/parse.
validation: Run `grep -rn 'keyevent_to_string\|keyutils.key_to_string\|keyutils.normalize_keystr' qutebrowser scripts tests` and expect no results.
Run `pytest tests/unit/keyinput`.
Run the pylint/flake8 tox envs to catch undefined names and unused imports.
Run scripts/keytester.py manually, or at least import-check it.

name: qutebrowser-normalize-backtab-in-keysequence-append-event
negative_constraints: Do not fix input-event normalization by renaming the key in the _key_to_string display mapping. That only changes the string representation and hides the real Qt key in error messages and key_data tests.
Do not keep using ev.key() after computing a normalized key. The final keys.append must use the normalized variable.
Do not drop the Shift modifier when converting Backtab to Tab. The result must be Shift+Tab, so that <Shift-Tab> bindings match and plain <Tab> bindings do not fire.
Do not apply the Backtab→Tab rewrite when Shift is absent. Only rewrite under ShiftModifier, as Qt delivers it.
Do not modify the is_printable Shift-stripping condition as part of this fix.
procedure: Locate the key-name mapping in qutebrowser/keyinput/keyutils.py::_key_to_string (the special_names string dict). Check whether a Qt key is being aliased to another key's display name, e.g. 'Backtab': 'Tab'. Such display-only aliases make different Qt keys indistinguishable by name only. They do not make bindings match.
Remove the display-name alias so that _key_to_string returns Qt's real name ('Backtab'). Keep naming 1:1 with Qt unless qutebrowser deliberately differs, as with 'Escape'.

Do the semantic normalization in KeySequence.append_event(ev), where the incoming QKeyEvent becomes a key|modifiers int. Read key = ev.key() once. If modifiers & Qt.ShiftModifier and key == Qt.Key_Backtab, rewrite key to Qt.Key_Tab. A user configures <Shift-Tab>, not <Shift-Backtab>.
Leave the existing Shift-stripping logic for printable keys unchanged. Build the appended value from the normalized local `key` (keys.append(key | int(modifiers))), not from ev.key().
Document the normalization in the append_event docstring next to the existing Shift-handling explanation.
Update tests/unit/keyinput/key_data.py: change Key('Backtab', 'Tab') to Key('Backtab') so the table expects Qt's own name.
Add or extend a test in tests/unit/keyinput/test_keyutils.py for append_event. Shift+Key_Backtab should produce the same KeySequence as parsing '<Shift-Tab>'. Plain Key_Tab should be unaffected.

trigger.task_type: Fix handling of Shift-Tab aka. Backtab

validation: Run pytest tests/unit/keyinput/ (test_keyutils.py and the key_data-driven tests).
Confirm _key_to_string(Qt.Key_Backtab) == 'Backtab' and _key_to_string(Qt.Key_Tab) == 'Tab'.
Confirm KeySequence().append_event(fake Shift+Key_Backtab event) == KeySequence.parse('<Shift-Tab>').
Manually, if possible: bind ':bind <Shift-Tab> ...' and press Shift-Tab in qutebrowser to check that it triggers.

name: qutebrowser-patch-release-version-bump
negative_constraints: Do not hand-edit `__version_info__` or replace it with a literal tuple.
Do not add pre-release or local suffixes such as '1.11.1-dev' or '1.11.1rc1'. `int(part)` would raise a ValueError at import time.
Do not change __copyright__, __author__, __description__ or other metadata during a version bump.
Do not bundle bug fixes, refactors or dependency updates into the release-bump commit.
Do not skip versions or regress the version number. The new version must be the immediate successor of the old one.
procedure: Open qutebrowser/__init__.py and find the single string assignment `__version__ = "X.Y.Z"`.
Change only that string literal to the target release version, for example "1.11.0" -> "1.11.1". Keep the format of three dot-separated integers.
Leave `__version_info__` unchanged. It is derived from `__version__` via `tuple(int(part) for part in __version__.split('.'))`.

Check whether the repository has other files that hard-code the old version, such as .bumpversion.cfg, misc/*.appdata.xml or doc/changelog.asciidoc. Only change them if the repository's release process puts them in the same commit. In the accepted evidence, only __init__.py changed.
Keep the release commit minimal: a one-line version change, with no functional code mixed in.
